page: UpCloud 24xCPU-96GB is a general-purpose server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 1920 GB local SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3748.58 and gzip compression reaching 36.22 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is strong, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 73962.01 and a bzip3 multi-threaded decompression speed of 290.89 GB/sec. Memory performance shows a clear tradeoff: cached small-block read bandwidth is strong at 3696.33 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the average tier, and the PassMark memory score is weak at 1832.2.

For specialized tasks, the server achieves top-tier performance in LLM inference for small 135M models, processing 3982.89 tokens/sec for prompts. Static web serving throughput is strong at 46.56 GB/sec. However, database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average levels. Given the shared CPU allocation and the weak uncached memory performance, this server offers a high-density resource profile for workloads like web serving, text processing, and light LLM inference, though it presents tradeoffs for memory-intensive database applications.
